{% raw %}
What the sign-in screens read and send. [How it is used](../authn-api.html).

The sign-in screen's API: what the screen offers for a pending sign-in, and the acts it sends. Unauthenticated and keyed by the pending sign-in's id; every act is bound to the browser's session cookie by a CSRF token. Answers name the next step; refusals are English and carry no error code. And the sign-out page's (#577): what a sign-out would end for the person the session names, and the act that ends it.

Every answer is checked against the model shown here before it is sent, and no answer carries a member its model does not list. A member shown as *any JSON* is one whose shape belongs to somebody else, and says whose. `.{key}` is a key that is data, and `[]` an element of a list.

## A refusal

Unless an operation below says otherwise, any status it does not list answers this:

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string |  |  |
| `error_description` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `next` | one of `refused` |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean |  |  |

## GET /authn-api/accounts

`getAccounts`

**The accounts this browser holds**

Each signed-in and remembered account of the browser's account set — key, subject, names, state, times, and whether it is the browser's default — never a sid or a token; `enabled` false and no accounts where authn.multipleAccounts is off. With it on, `anotherAccount` is where Sign in with another account starts: the user portal, asked to sign in again.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | query | string |  | Whom the page is about, where naming somebody is open (development mode and `logout.anyUser`), or the caller's own name; the browser's session otherwise. |
| `account` | query | string |  | With authn.multipleAccounts on (#561): one of this browser's signed-in accounts, by its key. |
| `login_hint` | query | string |  | With authn.multipleAccounts on (#561): the account the sign-out's account step preselects. |

## GET /authn-api/consent/{id}

`getConsent`

**What the OAuth consent screen asks**

The consent screen's view, as facts and no words: who is signed in, the application asking (its name and client_id), each scope outstanding and the permission it resolves to, each RFC 9396 authorization detail member by member, the limits a person may lower, what was already agreed, and the request's own parameters — and `csrf`. Refused (400) where nothing is pending under the id, or the browser's session is not the person it was asked of.

The door of the sign-in surface's `GET /oauth2/consent`.

## POST /authn-api/consent/{id}

`answerConsent`

**Allows or denies what the consent screen asks**

`action: allow` writes one oauthConsent value per scope onto the person's entry and records an RFC 9396 Allow for this one request, with any limit lowered (`lim_t0r<n>_<member>`, as the page draws them; a raised one is refused); `action: deny` records nothing. Either way the pending consent is spent and the answer names the authorization request to go back to.

The door of the sign-in surface's `POST /oauth2/consent`.

Sent with `Content-Type: application/json`, an `Origin` of this service and `X-CSRF-Token` — the `csrf` the page's view answered, bound to the browser's `sts_session` cookie.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | string | yes | The pending consent's id: a bearer capability, as the `consent` the consent screen was opened with, answered only to the browser whose session is the person asked. |

## GET /authn-api/logout

`getSignOut`

**Everything a sign-out would end**

The sign-out page's view, as facts and no words: every family of live session or credential this service holds for the person the browser's session names — or `username`, where naming somebody is open (a development test control) — each row with whether it can be ended and why not, and `csrf`. ## POST /authn-api/logout

**Signs out: everything, or what was ticked**

A `scope` of `global`, or no selection, ends everything the person holds; `select` ends those rows only, each looked up again now. The answer is the result, or the signed-out document that carries what the browser must still do.

## GET /authn-api/logout/accounts

`getSignOutAccounts`

**Which account a sign-out is for**

The sign-out's account step: this browser's signed-in accounts, each by its key, names and whether it is the browser's default — never a sid — the one `login_hint` names, preselected, and `csrf`. 400 where authn.multipleAccounts is off.

The door of the sign-in surface's `GET /logout/accounts`.

| `account` | query | string |  | With authn.multipleAccounts on (#561): one of this browser's signed-in accounts, by its key. |
| `login_hint` | query | string |  | With authn.multipleAccounts on (#561): the account the sign-out's account step preselects. |

## GET /authn-api/mfa/{id}

`getStep`

**What a second-factor or emailed-factor step's page shows**

The step's view for the page `page` names (`totp`, `webauthn`, `backup-code`, `password`, `setup`, `email-code`, `email-link`, `email-link-open`, `post-login`; the step's own where left out), as facts and no words: the person, the ways round the factor asked for, the set-up step's choice and its authenticator app's `otpauth:` URI, the passkey ceremony's description, an emailed factor's state — and `csrf`. Refused (400) where the page could never be drawn for the step: an expired step, a code page for somebody with no authenticator app, a passkey page for somebody holding no passkey (any key may answer the step since #1135; the authentication policy decides whether this use is open). `key` names the passkey a person chose where the passkey policy offers them one by one.

The door of the sign-in surface's `GET /authn/totp, /authn/webauthn, /authn/backup-code, /authn/password-factor, /authn/mfa-setup, /authn/email-code, /authn/email-link, /authn/email-link/open, /authn/post-login`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | string | yes | The second-factor or emailed-factor step's id: a bearer capability, as the `mfa` its page was opened with. |

## POST /authn-api/mfa/{id}/start-over

`startOver`

**Leaves a sign-in step and starts the sign-in over**

Every second-factor, set-up and emailed-factor page's Start over button. The step is ended with whatever it held (an emailed code, a link, an enrolment in progress), no session is started and no factor is counted, and the pending sign-in the step was minted from is put back under its id, so the request it carries completes after the person signs in again. `next: redirect` to the sign-in screen; a step that has already ended is refused (400).

The door of the sign-in surface's `POST /authn/totp, /authn/webauthn, /authn/backup-code, /authn/password-factor, /authn/mfa-setup, /authn/email-code, /authn/email-link, /authn/email-link/open`.

## POST /authn-api/mfa/{id}/webauthn/options

`passkeyStepOptions`

**Arms the passkey step's ceremony**

The step's challenge, the RP ID, the user (its handle and display name), the keys allowed and excluded and the passkey policy's options, for `navigator.credentials.create()` or `.get()` as `mode` says. `lane` (`classical` or `pqc`) chooses the lane a registration is made in where the realm offers both (#643): its handle, its algorithms and its exclude list. `algorithms: classical` (#944) arms a registration with the classical algorithms only, the retry `fallback.classical` says may be offered after an ML-DSA-first registration failed on the device; refused (400) where the realm forbids a classical passkey.

The door of the sign-in surface's `POST /authn/webauthn`.

## POST /authn-api/pending/{id}/accounts/select

`selectAccount`

**Continues as one of this browser's accounts**

The account is checked again: its session must still be live in this browser, and a demand for two factors it does not meet sends the person to sign in again as that account. A signed-out account goes to the sign-in with its name filled in. Every selection rotates the sts_accounts handle. 503 with Retry-After where the browser's accounts could not be read.

## GET /authn-api/wallet

`getWalletStart`

**What a wallet sign-in's start page needs**

Takes the start page's query — `authn` (a pending sign-in) or `mfa` (a second-factor step), `siop=1` for a self-issued ID Token, `enrol=1` to enrol one from a session (with `login_hint` naming which of the browser's accounts, and `did_act` one of a published DID's wallet acts, #1291) — and answers what is being started and `csrf`, after the refusals a start would meet. It creates nothing.

The door of the sign-in surface's `GET /authn/wallet`.

## POST /authn-api/wallet

`startWalletSignIn`

**Starts a wallet sign-in**

An OpenID4VP request bound to the pending sign-in (or the step, or the enrolment) and to this browser by the `sts_wallet_binding` cookie this answer sets; `go` names the wait page.

The door of the sign-in surface's `GET /authn/wallet`.

Sent with `Content-Type: application/json`, an `Origin` of this service and `X-CSRF-Token` — the `csrf` the page's view answered, bound to the browser's `sts_session` cookie.

**Request body**

|---|---|---|---|
| `authn` | ``, or string |  |  |
| `did_act` | ``, or string |  |  |
| `enrol` | ``, or one of `1` |  |  |
| `login_hint` | ``, or string |  |  |
| `mfa` | ``, or string |  |  |
| `siop` | ``, or one of `1` |  |  |
| `wallet` | ``, or string |  |  |

## GET /authn-api/wallet/{state}

`getWalletWait`

**What the wallet sign-in's wait page draws**

For the browser that started the transaction only: the Digital Credentials API request, the same-device link (`sameDevice`: the request under the scheme a wallet app registers for, `oid4vp.walletInvocation`), a configured web wallet's link (`webWallet`, or empty), the QR code's text where `oid4vp.signInCrossDevice` offers it, the seconds left and the poll's interval, and `csrf`.

The door of the sign-in surface's `GET /authn/wallet/wait`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | path | string | yes | The wallet sign-in's transaction: a bearer capability, answered to this browser only (its `sts_wallet_binding` cookie). |

## POST /authn-api/wallet/{state}/status

`walletStatus`

**Whether the wallet has answered, and the sign-in once it has**

The poll: `wait` until the wallet has answered, then the sign-in finished in this request — once, in the browser that started it, with the right `response_code` where one is carried.

The door of the sign-in surface's `GET /authn/wallet/wait`.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
